newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker amid dollar selloff.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker amid dollar selloff.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, as weakness in the Canadian dollar following this morning's tame Canadian inflation data weighed on prices.

"The currency, as we saw, took a dive on the weaker CPI figures. Knowing that the Bank of Canada is not going to raise rates makes holding Canadian dollars less attractive," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with financial analysis firm Technical Data.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.31 to C$119.14 to yield 6.532 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.51 percent. The gap in yields between the bonds moved to a positive spread of two basis points from a negative spread of one basis point at Monday's close.
Canada's dollar weakened following a report that the unadjusted July consumer price index rose 1.8. percent in the year. Core CPI rose 1.5 percent year-on-year.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast a 1.8 percent year-over-year rise in the all-items index and a 1.9 percent increase in the core CPI.
Canada's dollar ended the session sharply weaker at C$1.3944 (US$0.7171) from Monday's close at C$1.3882 (US$0.7203).

Dealers said a short squeeze affecting the Government of Canada's 4.0 percent bond due March 15, 1999 continues to distort the shape of the Canadian yield curve. The bond ended the session down C$0.13 to C$99.81 to yield 4.125 percent.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.18 to C$109.43 to yield 5.960 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.21 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 26 basis points at Monday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange fell 0.21 to 120.16 with 3129 contracts changing hands. A total of 2828 contracts traded on Monday.
